lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: labels and care symbols

objective: Learners learn to read five common care-label symbols (machine wash, hand wash only, no bleach, tumble dry, dry-clean only) by matching real or printed labels to their meanings, then correctly interpret three unfamiliar labels on their own.
scenario: An adult first shows the learner five real or printed care-symbol examples and explains what each one means and why it matters, then the learner finds and interprets three more labels — from their own clothes or a provided sheet — without being told the answer first.
safetyNotes: No bleach or other laundry chemical is handled in this lesson — symbols are studied on labels only.

simulationAlternative.description: If fewer than three additional real labels are available at home, the learner instead interprets three labels from a printed reference sheet of common care symbols, using the same explain-in-your-own-words method.

materials: five clothing items or printed care-symbol examples

tasks.directions: Before the model, look at one clothing label you already own. Which symbols on it do you recognize, and which are a mystery?

prompts.text: Describe what you recognize and what is unfamiliar.

tasks.directions: With your adult, go through the five common symbols (machine wash, hand wash only, no bleach, tumble dry, dry-clean only) one at a time.

prompts.text: I could restate what each of the five symbols means in my own words.
I named one real consequence of ignoring a specific symbol (like bleach damaging a dark item).
I asked about any symbol I still wasn't sure of.

tasks.directions: Find three more clothing labels on your own and write down what each one is telling you to do.

prompts.text: For each of your three labels, describe the symbol and its meaning.
Which of your three independent labels was hardest to interpret, and how did you figure it out (or who or what did you check with)?

remediation: If the learner confuses two visually similar symbols (like machine-wash-cool vs. hand-wash-only), reteach by placing the two symbols side by side and naming the one specific visual difference between them before retrying.
extension: Research (with an adult, from a reliable source) one care symbol not covered in this lesson and teach it back, in the learner's own words.
